Updates.title: Updates
Updates.description: Which version is installed and whether a newer release exists. Looking for updates does not install them.

upToDate.title: You are up to date
upToDate.description: {latest} is the latest stable release, as seen {when}.
upToDate.ahead: You are running {installed}, which is newer than the latest stable release ({latest}), as seen {when}.

updateAvailable.title: Version {latest} is available
updateAvailable.compatible: A compatible update. Take a backup before updating anyway.
updateAvailable.mayBreak: This update can include breaking changes. Read the release notes and take a backup before updating.
updateAvailable.candidate: You are running a release candidate of this version. The stable release is available.

checkFailed.title: Could not check for updates
checkFailed.description: {reason} That does not mean you are up to date: it means nobody knows.

notChecked.title: Not checked yet
notChecked.description: seotools has not looked for new releases yet. Check now, or turn on periodic checks.

development.title: Development build
development.description: This build does not come from a release. {version} is the last release it descends from, so it is not compared with new ones.

failures.timeout: GitHub did not answer in time.
failures.rate-limited: GitHub is limiting the requests of this server. Try again later.
failures.not-found: The release feed was not found; the repository may have moved.
failures.invalid-response: The answer from GitHub was not understood.

periodic.title: Periodic checks
periodic.description: Off by default: an installation does not contact anyone it was not told to.
periodic.label: Look for new releases once a day
periodic.hint: A check asks GitHub for the latest release of seotools. It sends nothing about your domains, your data or this installation; GitHub only sees the address your server connects from. It never changes anything by itself.

installing.title: Installing an update
installing.description: seotools never replaces its own container or asks for access to Docker. Docker or Dokploy does that, with the version you choose. Take a backup first: going back to an older image can require restoring it.

Crawl.progress: {done, number} of {total, number} URLs requested · {pages, plural, one {# page} other {# pages}} · {external, number} external

errors.alreadyRunning: This domain already has a crawl in progress.
errors.noPriorityUrls: There are no priority pages yet. Mark some in Pages first.
errors.invalidPriorityUrl: Enter a URL of {host}, like /pricing or https://{host}/pricing.
errors.invalidSchedule: Check the frequency, day and time of the schedule.

bulk.recheckLimit: Recheck without a crawl (up to {max, number} URLs)

errors.none: Choose at least one URL to recheck.
errors.invalid: None of those is a URL of {host}.
errors.tooMany: A recheck takes up to {max, number} URLs at a time. Choose fewer.
errors.noCrawl: There is no full crawl to compare with yet. Run one first.
errors.notInCrawl: The last full crawl does not have those URLs, or they are files for crawlers, which are refreshed from Crawl files.
errors.alreadyRunning: This domain is already rechecking URLs. Wait for it to finish, or cancel it.

active.title: Rechecking {count, plural, one {# URL} other {# URLs}}
active.waiting: It starts as soon as no crawl of this domain is running.
active.progress: {done, number} of {total, number} URLs requested again.

done.title: Rechecked {count, plural, one {# URL} other {# URLs}}
done.description: The last full crawl was not changed. Open the results to see what is fixed and what still needs a full crawl.

detail.title: Recheck
detail.scope: A recheck requests this URL again and judges what it answers on its own, without a crawl. The last full crawl is not changed. Findings that depend on other pages or on links (duplicates, links to this page, sitemaps, hreflang, redirect chains) can only be confirmed by a full crawl.
detail.waiting: This URL is waiting to be requested again.
detail.busy: Another recheck of this domain is under way. A domain rechecks one batch at a time.
detail.never: Not rechecked since the last full crawl.

rules.changedNote: The audit rules changed after this recheck, so exclusions and expected indexing may differ now. Recheck again to apply them.

detail.excluded: This URL is left out of the audit, so it has no findings of its own. It was still requested again.

found.title: Found in the recheck
found.none: The recheck found none of the issues it can settle.

fixed.title: No longer found
fixed.note: The crawl of {when} found these at this URL; the recheck does not.

notComparable.rules-changed: Not compared with the last full crawl: it was analysed under other audit rules, so a finding could appear or go away only because the rules moved.
notComparable.not-analysed: Not compared with the last full crawl: it has not been analysed for issues.

unchecked.title: Could not be checked from this URL alone

pending.title: Waiting for a full crawl
pending.none: The last full crawl found nothing at this URL that only a full crawl can settle.
pending.note: These depend on other pages or on links. They stay as the crawl of {when} found them: a recheck does not say whether they remain.

detail.checkedScope: Checked again: the HTTP response, page data, robots.txt and checks that depend only on this URL. Links from other pages, duplicates and sitemap membership still require a full crawl.
detail.evidenceNote: The response fields above and the recorded details below are from this recheck. Evidence samples from the full crawl are not reused here.

results.title: Recheck of {count, plural, one {# URL} other {# URLs}}
results.summary: {done, number} of {total, number} URLs requested again · started {when}

waiting.title: Waiting to start
waiting.description: A recheck waits while a crawl of this domain is running, and starts as soon as it ends.

results.scope: Compared with the last full crawl the URLs were picked from, which a recheck does not change. Findings that depend on other pages or on links are counted as waiting: only a full crawl says whether they remain.
results.notComparable: Some URLs were not compared with the crawl: it was analysed under other audit rules, or not analysed.
results.stale: The audit rules changed after some of these were rechecked. Recheck them again to apply the current rules.

jobs.title: Rechecks
jobs.description: Requests some URLs again after a fix, without a crawl, and judges what each one answers on its own. Start one from the pages table or the detail of a URL.

Pages.title: Pages
Pages.neverCrawled: This domain has not been crawled yet.

incomplete.title: The last crawl stopped at its URL limit
incomplete.description: It requested {urls, number} URLs and there were more. These figures do not cover the whole site.
incomplete.settings: Raise the limit in the crawl settings.

stats.note: Indexable pages are counted among every page crawled and only say what the crawl saw: they do not depend on the audit or on having findings. Issues, warnings and opportunities are counted among audited pages only, and a page counts in every group it has something of.
stats.unknownIndexability: {count, plural, one {# page has} other {# pages have}} too little data to tell.

chart.ariaLabel: Pages by what they have, after each full crawl
chart.empty: The history starts with the next full crawl: it is checked for issues when it ends.
chart.toggle: Show or hide in the chart

issues.title: Issues
issues.notChecked: The last full crawl has not been checked for issues. Run a new full crawl to see them here.
issues.noCrawl: Issues appear here once the domain has been crawled.

findings.empty: Nothing of this importance was found.

accepted.title: Accepted by a rule
accepted.help: The crawl still sees these, and a rule says they are expected. They are not pending, and they are not fixed: remove the rule and they count again.
accepted.viewAll: View every URL with an accepted finding

PagesDetails.title: Pages detail
PagesDetails.description: Every URL of the last full crawl. Select some to act on them together.
PagesDetails.neverCrawled: This domain has not been crawled yet. Run a full crawl from the pages overview.

viewHints.pages: URLs of this site that answered with HTML, whatever their status. These are the ones counted as pages.
viewHints.resources: URLs of this site that answered with something other than a page or a redirect: images, stylesheets, scripts, PDFs, robots.txt, sitemaps…
viewHints.redirects: URLs of this site that answered with a redirect (3xx).
viewHints.external: URLs on other sites linked from this one. Those of '<a>' links are requested once to find out whether they work; none counts as a page.
viewHints.all: Every URL the crawl recorded: pages, resources, redirects, external URLs, and URLs of this site that were not requested or never answered, which no other view lists. Filter by type to find those.
viewHints.other: Redirects, images, stylesheets, scripts, PDFs, robots.txt, sitemaps and URLs that did not answer.

PagesDetails.sortedAscending: Sorted ascending, click to sort descending
PagesDetails.sortedDescending: Sorted descending, click to remove the order
PagesDetails.selectAll: Select every URL on this page
PagesDetails.selected: {count, plural, one {# URL selected} other {# URLs selected}}

issueList.units: Each issue counts affected URLs. Category totals count findings; one URL can contribute several.

filters.label: Filters
filters.rule: Only the URLs decided by one rule.

unavailable.external: External URLs are not audited and have no type, so this filter does not apply to them.
unavailable.view: This view has a single type, so there is nothing to pick.
unavailable.no-audit-data: This crawl has no audit data yet, so this filter cannot apply.

PagesDetails.issueScope: Issues are looked for in every URL of the crawl, so this list is not limited to one view.

results.filtered: {matching, plural, one {# URL matches} other {# URLs match}} the filters, out of {total, plural, one {# URL} other {# URLs}} {scope}
results.internalOnly: These filters apply only to URLs on this site; external URLs are not included.
results.crawl: {total, plural, one {# URL} other {# URLs}} in the whole crawl

scopes.other: in the other URLs of the site

menu.pagesHint: One row per URL, with its state and how many findings it has.
menu.findingsHint: One row per finding, with its importance and what backs it.
menu.notAnalysed: This crawl has not been checked for findings.
menu.scope: Everything the filters leave, not only this page.

errors.missing: This crawl does not exist in this domain.
errors.noCrawl: This domain has no crawl with results to export yet.
errors.pruned: The results of this crawl were removed by the retention setting, so only its totals remain and there is nothing to export.
errors.notAnalysed: This crawl has not been checked for findings, so there are none to export.

UrlDetail.drawerDescription: What the crawl you are viewing found at this URL.
UrlDetail.notFound: This URL is not in the crawl you are viewing.
UrlDetail.noIssues: Nothing was found on this URL.
UrlDetail.notChecked: This crawl has not been checked for issues.
UrlDetail.loading: Loading the detail of the URL

audit.excludedNote: This URL is crawled and keeps all its data, but it is left out of the audit: it has no findings of its own. That does not mean it has nothing to fix.
audit.pendingNote: The audit configuration changed after this crawl was analysed. What is shown here may not reflect it yet.
audit.notAnalysed: This crawl was analysed before audit rules existed, or has not been analysed: the audit state of this URL is not known.
audit.noExplicitRules: No explicit rules apply to this URL.

UrlDetail.excludedFindings: Excluded from the audit: it has no findings of its own.
UrlDetail.findingsSummary: {count, plural, one {# finding} other {# findings}} · {high, number} high importance — view findings
UrlDetail.crawlFindingsNote: These findings belong to the selected full crawl. A recheck is shown separately below and does not replace them.

accepted.title: Accepted by a rule ({count, number})
accepted.note: The crawl still sees these. A rule says they are expected, so they are not pending, and they are not fixed.
accepted.expectation: A rule expects this URL not to be indexable.
accepted.origin: A rule expects this URL not to be indexable, so what it points at or what links to it is not news.
accepted.destination: A rule of the URL this one points at accepts it: {blockers}.
accepted.related: {total, plural, one {# URL it points at} other {# URLs it points at}}
accepted.elsewhereTitle: Rules of this URL act on other URLs ({total, number})
accepted.elsewhereNote: What a rule declares of this URL accepts these findings of the URLs that point at it. The first ones:

in.title: Incoming links
in.description: Pages of this crawl that link to this URL.
in.empty: No page of this crawl links to this URL.
in.note: A page counts once for each type of link it uses to reach this URL, however many times it repeats it.

out.title: Outgoing links
out.description: URLs this one links to, on this site and on other sites.
out.empty: The crawl recorded no links from this URL.
out.unread: The crawl did not read this URL, so what it links to is not known.
out.note: A URL counts once for each type of link this page uses to point at it, however many times it repeats it.

groupHelp.navigation: Links in the content of a page: the ones people click and search engines follow. Those marked rel="nofollow" say so.
groupHelp.resources: Scripts, stylesheets, images, media, frames and other files a page loads. Problems with them are reported under Issues whichever list is open.
groupHelp.declared: URLs that a page, a header or a sitemap names: canonical, hreflang, redirects, forms, structured data and others.

groupEmpty.navigation: No navigation links. Other types of link have some: see the counts above.
groupEmpty.resources: No resources. Other types of link have some: see the counts above.
groupEmpty.declared: No declared URLs. Other types of link have some: see the counts above.

UrlLinks.incomplete: This crawl stopped at its URL limit. Pages it never requested and URLs past the limit are not part of these links.

errors.unavailable: These links cannot be shown: the crawl is not available.
errors.pruned: The results of this crawl were removed, so its links are no longer stored.
errors.failed: The links could not be loaded. Try again.

UrlLinks.notRequested: The crawl did not request this URL, so it has no status.

IssueEvidence.unavailable: The examples are not available: this crawl was parsed before they were kept. Crawl the site again to see them.

units.related-urls: {total, plural, one {# other page} other {# other pages}}

labels.img-empty-alt: Images with an empty alt attribute
labels.img-long-alt: Images with a long alt text
labels.title-duplicate: Other pages with the same title
labels.description-duplicate: Other pages with the same meta description
labels.h1-duplicate: Other pages with the same H1
labels.content-duplicate: Other pages with exactly the same text
labels.content-near-duplicate: Other pages with almost the same text
labels.canonical-conflict: Canonicals declared, which do not agree
labels.canonical-relative: Canonicals that are not absolute URLs
labels.protocol-relative: Resources whose address has no scheme (//)
labels.unsafe-cross-origin-links: Links to another site in a new tab, without rel="noopener"

reasons.javascript-url: A javascript: address, which is not a page
reasons.scripted: No real address: a script handles the click

no-response.name: No response (internal)
no-response.description: A URL of this site that never answered: a network or DNS error, or a timeout.

server-error.name: Server error 5xx (internal)
server-error.description: A URL of this site answered with a server error.

client-error.name: Client error 4xx (internal)
client-error.description: A URL of this site answered that it does not exist or cannot be accessed.

redirect-loop.name: Redirect loop
redirect-loop.description: Following the redirects of this URL never reaches a page.

soft-404-confirmed.name: Probable soft 404 (title or heading)
soft-404-confirmed.description: Answers successfully with little text, and its title or main heading contains a not-found phrase. This is a local heuristic, not confirmation by Google; review the page.

soft-404-possible.name: Possible soft 404 (detected from content)
soft-404-possible.description: Answers 200, has little text, and what it has reads like a "not found" page. A guess from the content, not a certainty: review it.

redirect-chain.name: Redirect chain
redirect-chain.description: Redirects to another URL that also redirects. It should point straight at the final target.

refresh-redirect.name: Meta refresh or Refresh header redirect
refresh-redirect.description: Redirects from the HTML or with the Refresh header instead of a 3xx status code.

robots-blocked.name: Blocked by robots.txt
robots-blocked.description: robots.txt does not let Googlebot request this URL. This crawler requests it all the same to audit it.

redirect-3xx.name: 3xx redirect (internal)
redirect-3xx.description: A URL of this site that redirects. Links to it should point at its target.

broken-external-link.name: Broken external link
broken-external-link.description: A link to another site that does not answer or answers with an error. Answers typical of blocking bots, such as 403 or 429, are ignored.

directive-outside-head.name: Directive outside the '<head>'
directive-outside-head.description: There is a meta robots tag in the body of the page, where search engines may ignore it.

directives-conflict.name: Conflicting directives (indexing)
directives-conflict.description: The page says one thing and its opposite about indexing or following links, such as index and noindex.

directives-conflict-snippets.name: Conflicting directives (snippets or display)
directives-conflict-snippets.description: The page gives contradictory limits on how it is shown, such as nosnippet with max-snippet:50, or two different values of max-image-preview.

noindex.name: noindex
noindex.description: The page asks not to appear in search results.

nofollow.name: nofollow
nofollow.description: The page asks not to follow any of its links.

nosnippet.name: nosnippet / max-snippet:0
nosnippet.description: The page forbids any snippet, so it cannot be quoted in results or in Google's AI features. That hurts its visibility.

max-snippet-limited.name: Restrictive max-snippet (above 0)
max-snippet-limited.description: The page limits the snippet to a number of characters. The shorter the limit, the less of it can be quoted in results and AI answers. max-snippet:-1 places no limit and is not reported.

noimageindex.name: noimageindex
noimageindex.description: The page asks not to index its images, so they cannot appear in image search.

unavailable-after-expired.name: unavailable_after (date passed)
unavailable-after-expired.description: The page asked to stop appearing in results after a date that has already passed, so it is no longer shown.

unavailable-after-future.name: unavailable_after (future date)
unavailable-after-future.description: The page will stop appearing in results on the date it gives. Check that this is intended.

canonical-outside-head.name: Outside the '<head>'
canonical-outside-head.description: The canonical is in the body of the page, where search engines ignore it.

canonical-conflict.name: Conflicting canonicals
canonical-conflict.description: Declares several canonicals pointing at different URLs, so search engines may ignore them all.

canonical-not-indexable.name: Points at a non-indexable URL
canonical-not-indexable.description: The canonical leads to a URL that redirects, fails, has noindex, is blocked by robots.txt or canonicalises elsewhere, as the blockers shown say. Not reported when you declared every one of them as expected for that URL, or when this page is itself expected to be out of the index; a redirect or an error always is.

canonical-fragment.name: Contains a fragment
canonical-fragment.description: The canonical URL has a #fragment, which is not part of the address of a page.

canonical-missing.name: Missing
canonical-missing.description: The page does not declare a canonical.

canonicalised.name: Canonicalised to another URL
canonicalised.description: The canonical points at another URL, so search engines will index that one instead of this one.

canonical-relative.name: Relative
canonical-relative.description: The canonical is a relative path rather than a full URL.

canonical-repeated.name: Repeated with the same value
canonical-repeated.description: Declares the same canonical more than once.

sitemap-too-big.name: Sitemap over the limits (50,000 URLs or 50 MB)
sitemap-too-big.description: Search engines ignore what is past those limits. It should be split with a sitemap index.

sitemap-not-indexable.name: Non-indexable URL in the sitemap
sitemap-not-indexable.description: A sitemap lists this URL (its '<loc>') and something keeps it from being indexed, as the blockers shown say. An alternate (hreflang), image or video that an entry only names is not a listing. A crawl from before that was recorded cannot tell, and does not count a URL that a sitemap declared as an alternate.

indexed-not-in-sitemap.name: Indexed URL not in a sitemap
indexed-not-in-sitemap.description: A URL that a search engine has indexed and no sitemap lists. It takes a source that confirms indexing, such as Search Console, so nothing is reported until one is connected.

indexable-not-in-sitemap.name: Indexable URL not in a sitemap (indexing not confirmed)
indexable-not-in-sitemap.description: An indexable page that is in no sitemap. Nothing confirms that it is indexed.

hreflang-unreachable.name: Hreflang URL returns 4xx/5xx or does not answer
hreflang-unreachable.description: A hreflang points at a URL of this site that fails or never answers.

hreflang-redirect.name: Hreflang URL redirects
hreflang-redirect.description: A hreflang points at a URL of this site that redirects. It should point at the final URL.

hreflang-no-return.name: Missing return link
hreflang-no-return.description: The page the hreflang points at does not link back. Without a return link, search engines ignore the annotation. Not reported when either page is expected to be out of the index: its annotations are not read.

hreflang-invalid-code.name: Invalid language or region code
hreflang-invalid-code.description: The value is not an ISO 639-1 language with an optional ISO 3166-1 region. For example, the region of the UK is GB, not UK.

hreflang-outside-head.name: Outside the '<head>'
hreflang-outside-head.description: The hreflang is in the body of the page, where search engines ignore it.

hreflang-non-canonical.name: Return to a non-canonical URL
hreflang-non-canonical.description: A hreflang points at a URL whose canonical leads to another. Not reported when that URL is expected not to be indexable, or when this page is expected to be out of the index.

hreflang-noindex.name: Return to a noindex URL
hreflang-noindex.description: A hreflang points at a URL with noindex. Not reported when you require or allow that noindex (or expect the URL not to be indexable), or when this page is itself expected to be out of the index.

hreflang-same-language.name: Several entries for the same language
hreflang-same-language.description: The same language points at different URLs.

hreflang-no-self.name: Missing self-reference
hreflang-no-self.description: The hreflang annotations of the page do not include the page itself.

hreflang-no-x-default.name: Missing x-default
hreflang-no-x-default.description: The hreflang annotations of the page do not say which one to show by default.

title-missing.name: Missing
title-missing.description: The page has no title, or it is empty.

title-outside-head.name: Outside the '<head>'
title-outside-head.description: The title is in the body of the page.

title-multiple.name: Multiple
title-multiple.description: The page has more than one title.

title-duplicate.name: Duplicate
title-duplicate.description: Another indexable page has the same title.

title-too-long.name: Too long
title-too-long.description: Over 60 characters, an advisory review threshold. Display width varies; check clarity and how the title appears in results.

title-too-short.name: Too short
title-too-short.description: Under 30 characters, an advisory review threshold. A short title can be appropriate if it describes the page clearly.

description-multiple.name: Multiple
description-multiple.description: The page has more than one meta description.

description-outside-head.name: Outside the '<head>'
description-outside-head.description: The meta description is in the body of the page.

description-missing.name: Missing
description-missing.description: The page has no meta description, or it is empty.

description-duplicate.name: Duplicate
description-duplicate.description: Another indexable page has the same meta description.

description-too-long.name: Too long
description-too-long.description: Over 155 characters, an advisory review threshold rather than a search engine limit. Snippet length and content vary.

description-too-short.name: Too short
description-too-short.description: Under 70 characters, an advisory review threshold. Review whether it explains the page; shorter descriptions can be appropriate.

h1-multiple.name: Multiple H1
h1-multiple.description: The page has more than one H1.

heading-empty.name: Empty heading
heading-empty.description: There is a heading with no text.

heading-skipped-level.name: Non-sequential hierarchy
heading-skipped-level.description: It skips heading levels, for example from H2 to H4.

h2-missing.name: H2 missing
h2-missing.description: No H2 on a page with at least 300 words. This is a review heuristic; subsections are useful only when the content needs them.

h1-duplicate.name: Duplicate H1
h1-duplicate.description: Another indexable page has the same H1.

heading-too-long.name: Heading too long
heading-too-long.description: A heading exceeds 70 characters. This is an advisory review threshold; judge readability in context.

content-duplicate.name: Exact duplicate
content-duplicate.description: Another indexable page has exactly the same text. Check whether the duplication is intended and properly canonicalised.

content-near-duplicate.name: Near duplicate
content-near-duplicate.description: Another indexable page has nearly the same text.

content-placeholder.name: Placeholder text (lorem ipsum)
content-placeholder.description: The page contains placeholder text that was never replaced.

content-thin.name: Thin content
content-thin.description: Under 200 words, excluding menus, header and footer. This advisory threshold does not establish content quality or a minimum SEO word count; review whether the page meets its purpose.

img-no-alt.name: No alt attribute
img-no-alt.description: There are images with no alt attribute.

img-empty-alt.name: Review empty alt
img-empty-alt.description: Empty alt is valid for decorative images and does not require role="presentation". Review only whether any of these images convey information that needs alternative text; an empty alt alone is not an error.

img-too-heavy.name: Over 100 KB
img-too-heavy.description: The server declares an image over 100 KB. This is an advisory review threshold; suitable size depends on dimensions, format and use.

img-no-size.name: No width/height
img-no-size.description: Some images lack width or height attributes. Review layout stability; CSS or aspect-ratio may already reserve the needed space.

img-long-alt.name: Alt too long
img-long-alt.description: Alt text exceeds 100 characters. This is an advisory review threshold, not an accessibility limit; use the text needed to convey the image’s purpose.

json-ld-invalid.name: JSON-LD that does not parse
json-ld-invalid.description: There is a JSON-LD block with syntax errors, so search engines ignore it.

no-structured-data.name: No structured data
no-structured-data.description: The page has no JSON-LD, microdata or RDFa.

link-to-localhost.name: Link to localhost
link-to-localhost.description: The page links to localhost or 127.0.0.1, left over from a development environment.

uncrawlable-links.name: Uncrawlable internal links
uncrawlable-links.description: There are links that only work with JavaScript, such as javascript: or an '<a>' with no href, which search engines cannot follow.

only-nofollow-inlinks.name: Only receives nofollow links
only-nofollow-inlinks.description: Every link reaching this page is nofollow. Not reported for a page that is expected to be out of the index.

only-noindex-inlinks.name: Only linked from non-indexable pages
only-noindex-inlinks.description: Every link reaching this page comes from pages that will not be indexed. Not reported for a page that is expected to be out of the index.

orphan-in-sitemap.name: Orphan URL (only in the sitemap)
orphan-in-sitemap.description: No internal link to it was found within the scope of the crawl: only the sitemap leads to it.

no-outgoing-links.name: No outgoing internal links
no-outgoing-links.description: The page links to no other page of this site.

internal-nofollow-links.name: Internal links with nofollow
internal-nofollow-links.description: The page links to other URLs of this site with nofollow.

deep-page.name: High crawl depth
deep-page.description: It takes over 3 clicks from the home page to reach it.

anchor-empty.name: Empty anchor
anchor-empty.description: There are links with no text or anything else saying where they lead.

anchor-vague.name: Non-descriptive anchor
anchor-vague.description: There are links with text like "here" or "read more", which says nothing about the target.

url-multiple-slashes.name: Multiple slashes
url-multiple-slashes.description: The path contains two slashes in a row.

url-spaces.name: Contains spaces
url-spaces.description: The URL contains spaces encoded as %20.

url-tracking.name: Tracking parameters
url-tracking.description: The URL has parameters such as utm_source or gclid. Internal links should not carry them.

url-uppercase.name: Uppercase
url-uppercase.description: The path contains uppercase letters. /Page and /page are different URLs to a search engine.

url-repetitive-path.name: Repetitive path
url-repetitive-path.description: Part of the path repeats, typical of a badly written relative link.

url-internal-search.name: Internal search
url-internal-search.description: It looks like a results page of the internal search, which should not be indexed.

url-underscores.name: Underscores
url-underscores.description: The path uses underscores, which do not separate words for a search engine. Hyphens are better.

http-url.name: URL over HTTP
http-url.description: The page answers over HTTP without redirecting to HTTPS.

mixed-content.name: Mixed content
mixed-content.description: An HTTPS page loads resources over HTTP, which browsers may block.

insecure-form.name: Insecure form
insecure-form.description: There is a form that sends its data over HTTP.

missing-security-header.name: Missing security header
missing-security-header.description: The response leaves out a security header. They are all fixed in the same place, the server configuration.

unsafe-cross-origin-links.name: Unsafe cross-origin links
unsafe-cross-origin-links.description: There are links to other sites with target="_blank" and no rel="noopener".

protocol-relative.name: Protocol-relative resources
protocol-relative.description: There are resources loaded with URLs starting with //, with no scheme.

invalid-head-elements.name: Invalid elements in the '<head>'
invalid-head-elements.description: There are elements that cannot be in the '<head>'. They can end it early and make Google ignore the canonical or robots.

html-structure-broken.name: HTML structure that prevents reading indexing directives
html-structure-broken.description: A flaw in the structure of the HTML (an invalid element in the head, a misplaced or repeated head or body) left the robots meta, canonical or hreflang outside the '<head>', where search engines ignore them.

multiple-head-or-body.name: Multiple '<head>' or '<body>'
multiple-head-or-body.description: The document has more than one '<head>' or '<body>' tag.

document-too-big.name: Document over 2 MB
document-too-big.description: The HTML is over 2 MB, more than Googlebot reads of a page.

content-before-head.name: Content misplaced before the '<head>'
content-before-head.description: Something comes before the '<head>', which can make browsers end it early.

expected-indexable-blocked.name: Expected indexable but blocked
expected-indexable-blocked.description: You declared this URL should be indexable, but the crawl found something in the way: a noindex, a canonical to another URL, a robots.txt block or a redirect. The details name what it found. An error response is reported by its own response-code issue.

expected-not-indexable-but-indexable.name: Expected not indexable but indexable
expected-not-indexable-but-indexable.description: You declared this URL should not be indexable, but the crawl found nothing that stops it from being indexed: add a noindex, or point its canonical elsewhere.

noindex-required-missing.name: Required noindex is missing
noindex-required-missing.description: A rule requires this page to declare noindex, but the crawl read the page whole and found none. A page the crawl could not read whole, or did not request, is not reported.

nofollow-required-missing.name: Required nofollow is missing
nofollow-required-missing.description: A rule requires this page to declare nofollow for itself, but the crawl read the page whole and found none. A page the crawl could not read whole, or did not request, is not reported.

robots-block-required-missing.name: Required robots.txt block is missing
robots-block-required-missing.description: A rule requires robots.txt to block this URL, but the robots.txt that answered does not. A block only keeps crawlers from reading the URL: it does not take it out of a search engine’s index. A robots.txt that did not answer proves nothing, and is not reported.

sitemap-required-missing.name: Required sitemap listing is missing
sitemap-required-missing.description: A rule requires this URL to be in a sitemap, and none of the sitemaps lists it. It is only reported when every sitemap of the site was read in a crawl that finished; a recheck of some URLs cannot tell.

sitemap-forbidden-present.name: Listed in a sitemap where a rule forbids it
sitemap-forbidden-present.description: A rule forbids this URL to be in a sitemap, and a sitemap lists it.

Jobs.title: Scheduled jobs
Jobs.description: Run each type of crawl now or on a recurring schedule. A domain runs one crawl at a time.

typeDescriptions.full: Requests every URL of the site: from the home page, the sitemaps and everything linked anywhere, ignoring robots.txt and meta robots.
typeDescriptions.priority: Requests only the pages marked as priority in Pages, without following their links.

schedule.hourlyHint: Only the minutes count: it runs every hour at that minute.

lastOutcome.skipped-active: Last run skipped {when}: another crawl was in progress.
lastOutcome.skipped-empty: Last run skipped {when}: no priority pages marked.

DomainSettings.title: Settings
DomainSettings.description: Everything that can be configured for {host}.

CrawlSettings.title: Crawl settings
CrawlSettings.description: How crawls of {host} behave. Changes apply from the next crawl.

rendering.label: Page rendering
rendering.hint: A headless browser finds links that only exist after running JavaScript. It is not available yet.

modes.both: HTTP and headless browser, recommended (coming soon)

userAgent.label: User-Agent
userAgent.hint: Leave it empty to use the default one. Change it if a firewall blocks the crawler.

concurrency.label: Simultaneous requests
concurrency.hint: How many requests can be in progress at once.

requestsPerSecond.label: Requests per second
requestsPerSecond.hint: The most requests per second this domain receives.

timeout.label: Timeout (seconds)
timeout.hint: How long to wait for a URL before giving up on it.

maxRetries.label: Retries
maxRetries.hint: Extra attempts after a network error, 429 or 503.

maxUrls.label: URL limit
maxUrls.hint: Most URLs of the site a full crawl requests. Past it, the crawl ends as incomplete. Leave it empty for no limit, at the risk of a site with endless URLs.

retention.label: Crawl results to keep

hints.latest: Allows comparing crawls, with a bounded database size.
hints.current: The lightest option. Comparing crawls URL by URL will not be possible.
hints.all: Keeps all completed and incomplete crawl results; the database grows without limit.

retention.countHint: Older crawls keep totals only; their URL results, links and evidence are removed.

optionalFiles.label: Other crawl files
optionalFiles.hint: Files to check besides robots.txt, sitemaps and llms.txt. Checked as soon as you save, in every crawl and once a day.

feed.label: RSS / Atom feeds
feed.hint: Those the home page announces, or at the usual URLs.

opensearch.label: OpenSearch
opensearch.hint: The search description of the site.

indexnow.label: IndexNow
indexnow.hint: Tells search engines about changes at once. Its file is named after a key.

indexNow.label: Key
indexNow.hint: The file is named after the key, so it cannot be found without it. It has to be 8 to 128 letters, numbers or dashes.

errors.renderingUnavailable: That rendering mode is not available yet.
errors.userAgent: The User-Agent can only have plain characters, up to {max}.
errors.concurrency: Simultaneous requests must be between {min} and {max}.
errors.requestsPerSecond: Requests per second must be between {min} and {max}.
errors.timeout: The timeout must be between {min} and {max} seconds.
errors.maxUrls: The URL limit must be between {min} and {max}, or empty for no limit.
errors.retainCrawls: The number of crawls to keep must be between {min} and {max}.
errors.indexNowKey: The IndexNow key must be 8 to 128 letters, numbers or dashes.
errors.indexNowKeyRequired: Enter the IndexNow key, or turn IndexNow off.

refresh.crawlRunning: A full crawl is checking these files already.

CrawlFiles.neverFetched: Not checked yet. It takes a moment after adding a domain.
CrawlFiles.crawlRunning: A full crawl is running: it updates these files as it goes.

unreachable.title: The site did not answer the last check
unreachable.description: No request got an answer, so this is what was found before. It will be tried again in an hour.

requests.invalidDetail: It answers with something else, usually a web page.

raw.truncated: The file is larger than this: only the beginning is kept.

robots.title: robots.txt
robots.description: What the site tells crawlers they may request. The crawler of this app records it, but does not obey it.

missing.title: There is no robots.txt
missing.description: Crawlers take that to mean they may request everything.

unavailable.title: robots.txt could not be read
unavailable.description: The check could not read the file. See each request for the HTTP response or connection error; this does not establish that the file is absent.

invalid.title: The URL does not serve a robots.txt
invalid.description: It answers 200 with something else, usually a web page. Crawlers cannot find any rules in that.

site-blocked.title: The whole site is blocked for crawlers
site-blocked.description: The rules for every user agent disallow /. Unless a group names a crawler, it will not request anything.

too-large.title: The file is over 500 KiB
too-large.description: Google ignores whatever comes after that point, including any rules there.

no-sitemaps.title: It does not declare any sitemap
no-sitemaps.description: A Sitemap line is how crawlers that are not told otherwise find the sitemaps of a site.

origins-differ.title: Variants of the site serve different files
origins-differ.description: Rules apply per origin, so the same URL may be allowed on one variant and not on another. Compare them below.

syntax-issues.title: Some lines have problems
syntax-issues.description: Crawlers ignore what they cannot understand, so these lines probably do not do what was meant.

aiBots.title: AI bots
aiBots.description: Whether each one may crawl the site, going by these rules. Bots decide on their own whether to obey them.

groups.title: Rules by user agent
groups.description: Each group applies to the user agents above it.
groups.moreRules: And {count} more. See the file for all of them.

types.rule-outside-group: Rule with no User-agent before it

origins.title: Requests
origins.description: robots.txt applies per origin, so each variant of the site has its own.

sitemaps.title: Sitemaps
sitemaps.description: The lists of URLs the site offers crawlers, wherever they were found.

none.title: No sitemap was found
none.description: No readable sitemap was found. Check the request results before assuming that none exists.

not-declared.title: robots.txt does not declare the sitemaps
not-declared.description: They were only found by trying their usual locations. Crawlers may not do that.

declared-broken.title: robots.txt declares a sitemap that does not work
declared-broken.description: Crawlers are told to read it, and find an error instead.

empty.title: The sitemaps are empty
empty.description: They exist, but do not list any URL.

stats.urlsHint: Added up: a URL in two sitemaps counts twice.

table.title: Files
table.tried: {count, plural, one {# usual location was also tried and holds nothing, which is normal.} other {# usual locations were also tried and hold nothing, which is normal.}}

llms.title: llms.txt
llms.description: A summary of the site for AI models: what it is, and where to read about it. It is a proposal, not a standard that every AI product reads.

missing.title: There is no llms.txt
missing.description: It is optional, so this is not an error. Without it, AI models have to work out the site from its pages.

unavailable.title: llms.txt could not be read
unavailable.description: The check could not read the file. See each request for its response; its absence is not confirmed.

invalid.title: The URL does not serve an llms.txt
invalid.description: It answers 200 with something else, usually a web page.

no-title.title: It has no title
no-title.description: The format starts with a level 1 heading naming the site or project.

no-summary.title: It has no summary
no-summary.description: The format has a blockquote under the title, with a short summary.

no-links.title: It has no links
no-links.description: The format lists links to read further, under level 2 headings.

full.found: The full text for AI models, in one file: “{title}”, with {headings, plural, one {# heading} other {# headings}}.
full.missing: The optional companion with the full text in one file. This site does not have one.
full.unavailable: The optional companion could not be read. See the request results below.

extra.guessedNotFound: {count, plural, one {# usual location was tried and the home page does not announce any.} other {# usual locations were tried and the home page does not announce any.}}

disabled.title: {name} is not being checked
disabled.description: Turn it on in the crawl settings to request it in every crawl and once a day.

ads.name: ads.txt
ads.description: Who is authorized to sell the ad space of this site.

app-ads.name: app-ads.txt
app-ads.description: The same, for the apps of this developer.

security.name: security.txt
security.description: How to report a security issue (RFC 9116).

humans.name: humans.txt
humans.description: Credits for the people behind the site.

feed.name: RSS / Atom feeds
feed.description: The latest content, in a format that readers and crawlers follow.

opensearch.name: OpenSearch
opensearch.description: Lets browsers search this site directly.

indexnow.name: IndexNow key
indexnow.description: The file that proves this key may announce changes of the site to search engines.

invalid.title: Some lines are not valid
invalid.description: {count, plural, one {# line is} other {# lines are}} neither a record nor a variable: {lines}.

no-contact.title: It has no Contact field
no-contact.description: RFC 9116 requires it: it is the point of the file.

no-expiry.title: It has no valid Expires field
no-expiry.description: RFC 9116 requires one, so outdated information is not trusted forever.

expired.title: It has expired
expired.description: Past its Expires date, the file should no longer be trusted.

wrong-location.title: It is not where it should be

matches.title: The file holds this key
matches.description: Search engines will accept what is announced with it.

differs.title: The file holds something else
differs.description: It has to hold exactly the key, or search engines will refuse what is announced with it.

PrioritySettings.title: Priority pages
PrioritySettings.description: Pages of {host} that the priority crawl requests, with their most recent result from any crawl. Starring a page in the Pages list adds it here too.

IssueCatalog.noFindings: No findings recorded; applicability may be incomplete

typeHelp.warning: Something to review. It can matter as much as an issue: a security problem is a warning of high importance.

IssueCatalog.importanceHelp: The importance is independent of the type.

intent.notApplicable: Does not apply: not a page

outcome.met: The crawl saw what was expected.
outcome.robots-only: The only thing in the way is robots.txt. It keeps crawlers from reading the page, but it does not stop a search engine from listing the URL: it is no proof that it is out of the index.
outcome.unmet: The crawl saw the opposite of what was expected.
outcome.unknown: There is not enough data to say: the URL was not requested, the request failed, or it is not a page.

origin.removed: A rule that has been deleted since

audit.excludedByException: Excluded by an exception for this URL.
audit.includedByException: Included through an exception for this URL.

intent.indexableByException: Expected indexable by an exception for this URL.
intent.notIndexableByRule: Expected not indexable by the rule “{rule}”.
intent.notIndexableByException: Expected not indexable by an exception for this URL.

default.noindex: No rule applies: a noindex gets a finding.
default.nofollow: No rule applies: a nofollow of the page itself gets a warning.
default.robots: No rule applies: a robots.txt block gets a finding.
default.sitemap: No rule applies: an indexable page that no sitemap lists gets a low-priority warning.

condition.byException: {requirement} by an exception for this URL.

AuditState.technicalNote: This is what the crawl saw, not whether a search engine has indexed the URL, which a crawl cannot know.

outcome.met: The crawl saw what the rule asks.
outcome.unmet: The crawl saw the opposite of what the rule asks.
outcome.allowed: The rule accepts it either way.
outcome.unknown: The crawl could not tell: the page was not read whole, a file it depends on did not answer, or a sitemap from before the crawl recorded what it listed only names the URL.

rules.title: Audit rules
rules.description: What a rule says about the URLs it covers: whether they take part in the audit (excluded URLs are still crawled and keep their data, but get no findings of their own), what is required, allowed or forbidden of a noindex, a nofollow, a robots.txt block and a sitemap listing, and, as an advanced concept, whether they are expected to be indexable. A rule is a statement of intent: it never says whether a search engine has indexed a URL.
rules.default: By default, every URL is audited, nothing is asked of its conditions and every page is expected to be indexable.
rules.empty: Every URL is audited and no condition is required. Create a rule to exclude URLs that are still crawled, such as a shop’s cart, or to require, allow or forbid a noindex, a nofollow, a robots.txt block or a sitemap listing.

kinds.prefix: This path and everything below it

kindHelp.url: One URL, with its scheme, host, path and query. It takes precedence over any other rule: it is an exception for that URL.
kindHelp.path: This path and no other: /cart is not /cart/. It applies to the host and its www variant, over HTTP and HTTPS. Upper and lower case are different.
kindHelp.prefix: This path and what is below it by segments: /account covers /account, /account/ and /account/orders, but not /accounts. The longest prefix wins.

scope.label: Where the path is read
scope.literalHelp: The path is compared with the path of the URL as it is.
scope.sharedHelp: The same path inside each declared language directory and, if enabled, without one: /cart covers /cart, /es/cart, /en/cart… It does not translate slugs: /es/carrito and /en/cart need different rules.
scope.noLanguages: Declare the language directories first, in the “Language directories” tab. Until then a shared rule covers nothing.

query.label: Query string
query.valueHelp: Compared as written, in this order: a=1&b=2 and b=2&a=1 are different. Leave it empty for URLs without a query. A rule for a query beats one that ignores it.

form.reasonPlaceholder: Why? It is shown wherever this rule is what decides.
form.enabledHelp: A rule that is off is kept but decides nothing.
form.description: It applies to this domain, its www variant, over HTTP and HTTPS.
form.saved: Saved. The last crawl is being analysed again.

list.deleteDescription: The URLs it decides go back to what the other rules say. The last crawl is analysed again, without requesting anything from the site.
list.sharedWithoutLanguages: It covers nothing until the language directories are declared.

languages.title: Language directories
languages.description: The directories your site uses for its languages. Only the ones declared here are recognised: nothing is deduced from the first segment of a path. They are used by the rules shared between languages, and never change a URL.
languages.prefixesHelp: One per line or separated by commas. A directory is a single segment, such as /es or /pt-br. Upper and lower case are different.
languages.unprefixed: The default language has pages without a directory
languages.unprefixedHelp: Enable it for sites that mix paths with and without a directory (/cart and /es/cart). Leave it off when every language has one.
languages.saved: Saved. The last crawl is being analysed again.
languages.example: With /es, /en and /ca declared and paths without a directory enabled, a shared rule for /cart covers /cart, /es/cart, /en/cart and /ca/cart. It does not cover /fr/cart (not declared), /es/cartoon or /shop/es/cart.
languages.sharedRules: {count, plural, one {# rule uses the shared scope.} other {# rules use the shared scope.}}
languages.noSharedRules: No rule uses the shared scope yet.
languages.none: No directories declared: rules shared between languages cover nothing.

preview.title: Preview
preview.noResults: There is no full crawl with results to look at yet, so the preview cannot be worked out. You can save the rule: it applies to the next crawl.
preview.conflict: An enabled rule already has this exact selector: {rule}. Two rules of the same kind cannot cover the same URLs with the same specificity; edit that one or switch it off.
preview.matches: {count, plural, one {# URL of the last full crawl matches the selector.} other {# URLs of the last full crawl match the selector.}}
preview.matchesNone: No URL of the last full crawl matches the selector.
preview.changes: {count, plural, one {# URL would change its effective result.} other {# URLs would change their effective result.}}
preview.changesNone: No URL would change its effective result.
preview.overridden: {count, plural, one {# covered URL is decided by a more specific rule.} other {# covered URLs are decided by a more specific rule.}}
preview.note: This only shows the URLs the last full crawl knows (finished {when}). The rule also applies to URLs found in later crawls.
preview.noteUnknown: This only shows the URLs the last full crawl knows. The rule also applies to URLs found in later crawls.
preview.scanned: {count, plural, one {# URL} other {# URLs}} looked at.
preview.inactive: This rule is switched off, so it decides nothing yet. The matches show what it would cover once it is on.

pending.title: The results are pending an update
pending.description: The audit configuration changed after the last full crawl was analysed. The worker is analysing it again from what it stored, with no new requests to the site. Until then the figures and findings do not reflect the current configuration.

failed.title: Analysing the last crawl again failed
failed.description: The results still reflect an older configuration. The error was: {error}

status.noCrawl: Rules apply to the next full crawl: there is no full crawl with results to analyse yet.

errors.value: Choose a value that exists for each thing the rule says.
errors.kind: Choose what the rule applies to.
errors.scope: Choose where the path is read.
errors.external: Only URLs of this domain can be configured: the domain, its www variant, over HTTP or HTTPS.
errors.path: A path starts with / and has no query, fragment or backslash. The query goes in its own field.
errors.query: That is not a valid query. Leave out the # and what follows it.
errors.conflict: Another enabled rule of this kind already covers exactly the same URLs.
errors.limit: This domain has reached the limit of rules.
errors.languagesPrefix: A directory is a single segment of letters, digits, - or _, such as /es or /pt-br.

urls.urls: Choose between 1 and 200 URLs of the domain.
urls.external: Only URLs of this domain can be configured.

errors.statements: Choose at least one thing for the rule to say: whether the URLs take part in the audit, a condition or the expected indexing.

AuditDialog.title: Configure audit
AuditDialog.description: {count, plural, one {# URL selected.} other {# URLs selected.}} It is saved as an exception for each URL, and the last full crawl is analysed again in the background, with no requests to the site.
AuditDialog.descriptionOne: It is saved as an exception for this URL, and the last full crawl is analysed again in the background, with no requests to the site.
AuditDialog.multipleHint: Nothing is changed unless you choose it. “No change” leaves each URL as it is; “According to the rules” removes the exception of the URLs, so they take what the rules say.
AuditDialog.reasonPlaceholder: Why? It is shown wherever this decides.
AuditDialog.reasonKept: Left empty, each exception keeps its own reason.

stamp.prunedHint: Only the totals of this crawl remain: its results per URL were removed by the retention setting.
stamp.catalogOlderHint: Its findings were worked out with an earlier version of the issue catalog than the one in use now.

picker.label: Crawl
picker.option: {when} · {status}{coverage, select, pruned { · results pruned} other {}}{latest, select, yes { · latest} other {}}

banner.viewing: You are viewing the crawl of {when}, not the latest one.
banner.configBehind: Analysed under: {config}. In force now: {current}. An earlier crawl keeps the rules it was analysed with, so its results are not recalculated.
banner.incomplete: Partial coverage: this crawl did not complete. Findings may be missing.

details.detailsDescription: Every URL of the chosen full crawl, as that crawl saw it. Select some to act on them together.
details.prunedBody: The results per URL of this crawl were removed by the retention setting. Only its totals remain: {pages} pages and {urls} URLs were found. Choose a crawl that still has its results.
details.prunedSettings: Change how many crawls keep their results

list.title: Crawl history
list.description: Every full crawl of this domain that finished with results, newest first. A crawl keeps the audit configuration it was analysed with, and its results per URL until the retention setting removes them.
list.empty: This domain has no finished full crawl yet. Run one from the pages overview.

compare.title: Compare two crawls
compare.description: Choose the crawls to see what was discovered, not seen again and changed between them.

list.retention: How many crawls keep their results per URL is set in the crawl settings; older ones keep only their totals.
list.capped: Showing the newest {count} crawls. Older ones are not listed.

url.title: History of this URL
url.description: What each retained full crawl recorded of this URL, newest first ({count, plural, one {# crawl} other {# crawls}}). A crawl without results says so; it is never read as the URL being absent.
url.empty: No crawl has results for this URL.
url.prunedHint: Only the totals of this crawl remain, so it cannot say what this URL looked like.
url.prunedRow: The results of this crawl were pruned
url.notSeen: This crawl did not find the URL

timeline.title: Findings over time
timeline.description: Each square is a crawl, oldest first. A finding is called new, resolved or reappeared only when the crawls on both sides could have reported it under the same issue catalog and audit rules.
timeline.legend: Red: reported. Green: not reported by a crawl that could have reported it. Dashed: the crawl cannot say (pruned, not analysed, URL not found or not requested, excluded from the audit, or a different catalog or configuration).

CrawlCompare.title: Compare crawls
CrawlCompare.description: What changed between two full crawls, read from what they stored. Nothing is requested from the site. Where the evidence does not say why something changed, the page does not either.
CrawlCompare.needTwo: Comparing needs two finished full crawls of this domain. Run another crawl first.
CrawlCompare.sameCrawl: Both ends are the same crawl. Choose two different crawls.

totals.title: Totals
totals.description: Totals survive pruning, so they can always be compared. A difference in the totals has the same possible causes as the changes below: the site, the crawl, or the audit rules.

hints.added: URLs the later crawl found and the earlier one never did. The site may have gained them, or the earlier crawl may not have reached them.
hints.addedIncomplete: The earlier crawl stopped at its URL limit, so it never reached many URLs. Some of these may have existed all along.
hints.missing: URLs the earlier crawl found and the later one did not. They may have been deleted, stopped being linked or listed in a sitemap, or not been reached: this does not say which.
hints.missingIncomplete: The later crawl stopped at its URL limit, so these are most likely URLs it did not reach. Nothing here says they were removed.
hints.status: URLs both crawls requested that answered differently: another status code, another kind of URL or another redirect target.
hints.title: URLs both crawls requested whose title changed. Compared exactly, capitals included.
hints.canonical: URLs both crawls requested whose declared canonical changed.
hints.robots: URLs both crawls requested whose meta robots or X-Robots-Tag changed.
hints.gained: URLs both crawls requested where the later crawl reports findings the earlier one did not. The badge says what the evidence supports: new or reappeared, or not attributed when the rules, the catalog or the crawl itself changed.
hints.lost: URLs both crawls requested where the earlier crawl reported findings the later one no longer does. Resolved only when nothing but the site can explain it; a URL that is no longer audited is shown as excluded by rule, never as resolved.

CrawlCompare.unrequested: {count, plural, one {# URL was found by both crawls but not requested by at least one of them, so it is not compared.} other {# URLs were found by both crawls but not requested by at least one of them, so they are not compared.}}

table.empty: No URLs changed in this way.
table.findingsUnavailable: Findings cannot be compared for these crawls.
table.samePersistent: {count, plural, one {# finding reported by both} other {# findings reported by both}}

findingKinds.newHint: Reported by the later crawl and not by the earlier one, which could have reported it under the same catalog and rules.
findingKinds.reappearedHint: Reported, then not reported by a crawl in between that could have reported it, then reported again.
findingKinds.resolvedHint: Reported by the earlier crawl and not by the later one, which could have reported it under the same catalog and rules.
findingKinds.excludedHint: The later crawl no longer audits this URL, so its findings are gone by policy. It does not mean they were resolved in the site.
findingKinds.auditedHint: The earlier crawl left this URL out of the audit, so this finding is not new: it was not being looked for.
findingKinds.unverifiedHint: The findings differ, but this is not shown as new or resolved because: {reasons}.
findingKinds.acceptedHint: The later crawl still sees it, and a rule says it is expected. It was not fixed.

reasons.not-seen: the crawl does not have the URL
reasons.not-requested: the URL was found but not requested
reasons.excluded: the URL is excluded from the audit
reasons.participation: the analysis did not keep whether the URL was audited
reasons.incomplete: a crawl stopped at its URL limit and this finding depends on other pages
reasons.audit: the audit configuration or the expectation for the URL differs

title.base: The earlier crawl no longer has its results
title.target: The later crawl no longer has its results
title.both: Neither crawl has its results any more

pruned.description: Retention removed the results per URL, so only the totals can be compared. Choose crawls that still have their results, or raise the number of crawls kept in the crawl settings.

title.base: The earlier crawl was not analysed
title.target: The later crawl was not analysed

unanalysed.description: Without an analysis there are no findings to compare. URLs and how they answered (status, title, canonical, robots) are still compared.

title.base: The earlier crawl was analysed before the audit state per URL was kept
title.target: The later crawl was analysed before the audit state per URL was kept
title.both: Both crawls were analysed before the audit state per URL was kept

legacy.description: It is not known which URLs were left out of the audit then, so a finding that is not there cannot be read as fixed. Those changes are shown as not attributed.

catalog.title: The crawls were analysed with different issue catalogs
catalog.description: A finding that appears or goes may come from a check that changed, not from the site. Such differences are listed as unverified, never as new or resolved.

audit.title: The crawls were analysed with different audit configurations
audit.description: Exclusions, expected indexing or language directories changed between them. A URL that stopped being audited is shown as excluded by rule, not resolved. Findings that depend on other pages are not called new or resolved; findings that only depend on the page itself still are, unless the expectation for that URL changed.

title.base: The earlier crawl stopped at its URL limit
title.target: The later crawl stopped at its URL limit
title.both: Both crawls stopped at their URL limit

incomplete.description: URLs it did not reach are not missing, and findings that look at other pages (duplicates, inbound links, redirects) are not called new or resolved for it.

audit.label: Audit participation
audit.help: Whether these URLs take part in the audit. Excluded URLs are still crawled and keep their data, but get no findings of their own.

conditions.title: Conditions
conditions.noneUrl: No condition is set. Add one to require, allow or forbid a noindex, a nofollow, a robots.txt block or a sitemap listing.
conditions.noneRule: This rule sets no condition. Add one to require, allow or forbid a noindex, a nofollow, a robots.txt block or a sitemap listing.
conditions.unknown: If the crawl could not tell (a page it could not read whole, a robots.txt or a sitemap that did not answer), no finding is raised and the condition is not counted as met.

noindex.label: Noindex
noindex.default: By default, a page that declares noindex gets a finding.

help.required: A finding is raised when the page does not declare noindex. Pages that point at it (canonical, hreflang) are not told about that noindex.
help.allowed: The page may declare noindex or not: no finding for the noindex either way, and pages that point at it (canonical, hreflang) are not told about it.
help.forbidden: A finding is raised when the page declares noindex.

nofollow.label: Nofollow
nofollow.default: By default, a page that declares nofollow for itself gets a warning.

help.required: A finding is raised when the page does not declare nofollow.
help.allowed: The page may declare nofollow or not: no finding for it either way. Links marked rel="nofollow" are not affected.
help.forbidden: A finding is raised when the page declares nofollow.

robots.label: Blocked by robots.txt
robots.default: By default, a URL blocked by robots.txt gets a finding.

help.required: A finding is raised when robots.txt does not block the URL. A block only keeps crawlers from reading it: it does not take the URL out of a search engine’s index. Canonicals that lead to it are not told about the block.
help.allowed: The URL may be blocked by robots.txt or not: no finding for the block either way, and canonicals that lead to it are not told about it.
help.forbidden: A finding is raised when robots.txt blocks the URL.

sitemap.label: Listed in a sitemap
sitemap.default: By default, an indexable page that no sitemap lists gets a low-priority warning.

help.required: A finding is raised when no sitemap lists the URL (an alternate or an image that an entry only names is not a listing). It needs a complete crawl: a recheck of some URLs cannot tell.
help.allowed: The URL may be listed in a sitemap or not: no finding for its absence. A listed URL that cannot be indexed is still reported.
help.forbidden: A finding is raised when a sitemap lists the URL.

advanced.title: Advanced: expected indexing
advanced.help: The expectation is about the URL as a whole: a noindex, a canonical to another URL, a redirect, an error or a robots.txt block can each keep it from being indexed. The conditions above are about one directive or file each, and never about whether the URL is in a search engine’s index.

help.default: Unless a rule says otherwise, every page is expected to be indexable.
help.indexable: The crawl is checked for what stands in the way of indexing the URL.
help.not-indexable: A noindex is fine; being indexable is not. It is not the same as requiring a noindex. Pages that point at it are not told about its noindex or a canonical elsewhere; a robots.txt block is still reported.

AuditStatements.relationsNote: This also accepts findings of the URLs that point here (canonical, hreflang). Accepted findings are not fixed: they stay visible as accepted by a rule.

FindingHelp.title: Edit the page template to provide one descriptive title in the head. Make it specific to this page and review its length and any duplicates.
FindingHelp.response-codes: Inspect the response and redirect destination. Fix unintended server errors, broken URLs or redirect chains at the server, then check the URL again.
FindingHelp.indexing-intent: Compare the observed blockers with the intended indexing policy. Adjust the relevant directive or sitemap entry; change the rule only if the declared expectation is wrong.
FindingHelp.directives: Review both the HTTP X-Robots-Tag header and the robots meta tags. Make them consistent with the intended policy and place HTML directives in the head.
FindingHelp.canonicals: Review the canonical declarations and their destination. Use a consistent absolute URL without a fragment, and confirm that the chosen destination is the intended canonical page.
FindingHelp.sitemaps: Review the sitemap file and the affected entries. Align listed URLs with your sitemap policy, fix invalid or oversized files, then run a full crawl to check site-wide findings.
FindingHelp.hreflang: Review the affected language cluster. Correct language codes and destinations, use consistent canonical URLs and return links, then run a full crawl.
FindingHelp.meta-description: Provide one useful description in the head that reflects the page content. Review its length and avoid reusing the same description on different pages.
FindingHelp.headings: Review the heading hierarchy in the page template. Use descriptive, nonempty headings that reflect the structure of the content.
FindingHelp.content: Review the rendered content and any related pages in the evidence. Replace placeholders, add useful original content, or consolidate pages that serve the same purpose.
FindingHelp.images: Inspect the affected images in the page template. Add useful alt text for informative images, keep decorative images empty, and review dimensions and file weight.
FindingHelp.structured-data: Review the page’s JSON-LD. Fix syntax errors and use structured data appropriate to the visible content; validate it after editing.
FindingHelp.links: Review the affected links and their source pages. Use reachable HTTP(S) destinations and descriptive anchors, and add useful internal navigation where needed. Run a full crawl for findings about incoming links.
FindingHelp.urls: Review URL generation and internal links. Choose a stable, readable URL format and, if an address must change, update links and configure the appropriate redirect.
FindingHelp.security: Review the affected resources, forms, links or HTTP headers. Use HTTPS destinations and apply the relevant browser security protections, checking that the change preserves site functionality.
FindingHelp.html: Inspect the returned HTML and its template. Correct the document structure, keep metadata inside a valid head and reduce excessive document size where relevant.
FindingHelp.robots-blocked: If this URL should be crawlable, edit the matching robots.txt rule for the audited bot. If the block is intentional, declare it in the audit rules; a block does not prove that the URL is absent from search results.
FindingHelp.no-response: Check DNS, TLS, server availability and timeout settings. Restore access for the configured crawler User-Agent, then recheck the URL.
FindingHelp.client-error: Restore the intended resource or correct the links pointing to it. If it moved, redirect to the relevant replacement; if the error is intentional, review the audit policy.
FindingHelp.soft-404-confirmed: Check whether the page is actually missing. Return a real 404/410 for removed content, or restore useful content and remove misleading error signals.
FindingHelp.soft-404-possible: Inspect the page manually to confirm whether it is an error page. If so, return an appropriate error status; otherwise review the content that resembles an error message.
FindingHelp.broken-external-link: Check the linked external destination and update or remove the broken link on its source pages. Run a full crawl to check external links again.
FindingHelp.refresh-redirect: Review the refresh declaration. If the move is permanent, prefer an HTTP redirect to the final destination and update internal links.
FindingHelp.noindex: If the page should be indexable, remove the noindex directive from the HTML and HTTP headers. If it is intentional, declare the intended policy in the audit rules.
FindingHelp.canonicalised: Confirm that the declared canonical is the intended preferred URL. If this page should stand on its own, correct the canonical; otherwise align internal links and the audit expectation with the preferred page.
FindingHelp.noindex-required-missing: Add a noindex directive in the page head or X-Robots-Tag header if this requirement is correct. Otherwise edit the rule that requires it, then recheck.
FindingHelp.nofollow-required-missing: Add the required nofollow directive in the page head or HTTP header, or correct the rule if links should be followed. Nofollow does not prevent indexing.
FindingHelp.robots-block-required-missing: Add the intended block in robots.txt for the audited bot, or correct the rule that requires it. A robots.txt block does not guarantee removal from the index.
FindingHelp.sitemap-required-missing: Include this URL as an entry in a sitemap that the crawler can read, or correct the rule requiring it. Run a full crawl to verify membership.
FindingHelp.sitemap-forbidden-present: Remove the URL entry from the affected sitemaps, or correct the rule if it should be listed. Run a full crawl to verify the change.

archive.title: Archive {host}?
archive.description: Its data is kept and stays readable. Scheduled crawls and refreshes of its icon and files stop, a crawl or recheck in progress is cancelled, and its settings cannot change until you restore it.

move.title: Move {host}
move.label: New company
move.results: Its crawls, results, rules and schedules move with it unchanged.

access.unchanged: Access does not change: every signed-in user can see it before and after the move, because access is not set per company yet.

changeSite.title: Change site
changeSite.description: A domain's address cannot be edited, because its results belong to that site. To track a new site, add a new domain and archive this one.

delete.companyLead: This permanently deletes the company with {domains}: {hosts}, and:
delete.companyLeadEmpty: This permanently deletes the company, which has no domains.
delete.nothingStored: No crawls, results, rules or schedules are stored for it.
delete.keepHistory: To keep its history, archive it instead.

usage.priorityUrls: {count, plural, one {# priority URL} other {# priority URLs}}
usage.crawlFiles: {count, plural, one {# crawl file} other {# crawl files}}

errors.sameCompany: The domain already belongs to that company.
errors.confirmMismatch: What you typed does not match.
